answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 3 times its size, so a group of 27 keys loses far more than 27 single identities would. The glacier graph is rebuilt each epoch, and hence the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the wharf audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the relic checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 7 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
